(This evening through Wednesday)...
Issued at 309 PM EDT Wed Oct 28 2026

Tonight through Thursday night...

A broad area of surface high pressure extending from New England 
into the Srn Appalachians will slowly give way to a low pressure 
area and cold front moving from the northern Plains into the western 
Great Lakes region. Winds will remain light southerly overnight with 
lows in the upper 40s to lower 50s area wide. On Thursday, expecting 
another day of large diurnal changes in temps, with temperatures 
quickly rising into the 70s by noon thanks to a shallow inversion, 
increasing SW winds and steep low level lapse rates. Thermal ridge 
takes aim at central IN with +13C at 850mb by 18Z. High temperatures 
as a result are expected to be 15-20 deg above normal from the upper 
70s to near 80. For reference the record high for Indianapolis on 
Thursday is 82 set in 1927. 

As the cold front pushes south from northern Indiana, sufficient 
moistening of the BL combined with frontal ascent suggests the 
potential for light rain showers to occur over northern portions of 
central Indiana during the late afternoon/evening. NAM is the most 
bullish of the suite of model guidance, but inspection of the NAM 
forecast soundings suggest this may be due to the normal NAM over 
saturation bias in the BL. It does appear prudent to carry slight 
chance PoPs given the degree of available moisture (dewpts in the 
mid-upper 50s) and fairly strong convergence along the front. Poor 
mid level lapse rates owing to mid level subsidence in the wake of 
the primary shortwave trough axis moving into the eastern Great 
Lakes will preclude any TS chances. 

Friday through Friday Night...

The surface frontal boundary is expected to undergo frotolysis 
across the Ohio Valley early on Friday. The presence of upper 
ridging building in from the west ahead of weak shortwave trough 
moving through the southern Plains, combined with surface high 
pressure centered over the Great Lakes, will lead to much more 
quiescent weather on Friday across central Indiana. By Friday night, 
the lead shortwave is expected to approach the MS valley. There is 
some signal for enough mid level saturation to occur where the 
greatest height falls/weak FGEN forcing occur, that some light 
showers will be possible across northern zones Friday night. 

Saturday through Sunday...

As the lead shortwave trough moves through the upper ridge, with 
limited low level response seen on guidance, the consequent effect 
will be widespread mid-high level cloud cover on Saturday with 
little to no precip chances expected except early in the far north. 
There is a high degree of model uncertainty with regards to the 
precip potential for Sat night into Sunday. The GFS has a much 
stronger secondary shortwave (current well west of the Baja CA 
coast) moving across the MS valley into the Ohio Valley Sat night 
into Sunday. In particular the GFS has a much stronger 850 mb jet 
that develops over the Gulf Coast, somewhat convectively enhanced, 
but also supported by barrier jet processes on the fringes of the 
surface ridge in the Carolinas. As a result, more rapid moisture 
return by the GFS would support greater QPF across central Indiana. 
However, ensemble data and the OP Euro are much weaker with the mass 
fields and consequent QPF amounts and coverage through Sunday. In 
fact the OP Euro has almost no precip for central Indiana as the 
shortwave trough undergoes greater deamplification. For now, will 
play the middle ground with moderate PoPs for the entire forecast 
area Sat night into Sunday.

Monday through Wednesday...

Not too unsurprising, the differences in guidance becoming amplified 
with the upcoming phasing/pattern amplification over the western and 
central CONUS early next week. The GFS is much more bullish with a 
large closed cyclone developing over the Plains by Monday with 
strong phasing of the northern and southern streams/shortwaves. 
While the Euro and other ensemble guidance keep the streams slightly 
out of phase and pattern more progressive. As a result, the forecast 
leans more towards the progressive solutions with rainfall chances 
increasing by Tuesday-Wednesday. Moisture return and quality of 
instability are the main questions regarding TS coverage and severe 
potential this far out. However, kinematics will be favorable for 
some potential severe if instability is higher than currently 
progged.
